title: A row can push its contents to its two ends
goal: A stack that has been given a size can spread the room it has left between its rows instead of holding one fixed gap, which is how a nav bar with a logo on the left and buttons on the right is built.
notes: Sources/PhotonzCore/GroupLayout.swift holds a single CGFloat gap with usedGap; the spread case wants gap to become a small enum or an optional so Codable can stay backward compatible. Placement runs in GroupFlow.swift. No decision card: this is an option on the Gap row the user already sets, inside the auto layout epic they promoted on 2026-09-03, not a new surface. The starter nav bar still holds the size it was drawn at, see queue/audits/2026-09-04-ui-hug.json.
acceptance: The Gap row can be set to spread the leftover room instead of a number, on a stack that has a size of its own
A stack that hugs its contents has no leftover room, so the choice is not offered there and says why in one line rather than sitting dead
With two rows the room goes between them, with three it is shared equally, and the padding on the sides is respected
Turning it back to a number restores the number that was there before
Ships behind next-auto-layout. To see it: open Photonz Next, drop the starter nav bar, set its width to 640, set its Gap to spread, and watch the pieces move to the two ends
Tests in PhotonzCore cover two rows, three rows, both directions, padding and the hug case before the app code is written
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
